text.en: Transgenesis · Knockout · Dolly · Hybridoma · Gene therapy · CRISPR · Markers

Seventeen diagrams and flow charts for Unit III: how transgenic and knockout mice are made, how Dolly was cloned, how HAT selects hybridomas, the logic of gene therapy and CAR-T, how CRISPR cuts and repairs DNA, and how markers and fingerprints are read.

text.en: A transgenic animal carries a foreign gene (transgene) in its genome and passes it on.

Transgenic animal
An animal whose genome contains a stably integrated foreign gene (transgene) that is transmitted through the germ line.

labels: Typical transgene construct (linear DNA for injection)
Example: β-lactoglobulin or αS1-casein promoter + human gene → protein secreted in milk.
Metallothionein promoter (zinc inducible) + growth hormone gene gave the “super-mouse” (Palmiter and Brinster, 1982).

title.en: Knockout Mice and Dolly the Sheep

text.en: Two classical landmarks: targeted gene disruption in mice (Capecchi, Evans, Smithies; Nobel 2007) and cloning from an adult cell (Wilmut, Campbell 1996).

labels: Random integration keeps tk: ganciclovir kills those cells.
Correct targeting loses tk but keeps neo: resistant to G418 and ganciclovir.

caption.en: Fig. 4. From ES cell to knockout mouse.

text.en:
**PG focus**
• Conditional knockouts (Cre-loxP) restrict gene deletion to a tissue or time.
• Dolly’s mitochondrial DNA came from the egg donor, so she was a nuclear clone, not a complete genetic copy.
• Related: embryonic cloning (embryo splitting) differs from SCNT.

title.en: Animals as Bioreactors, Superbug and Bioremediation

text.en: Transgenic animals can make drugs in milk; engineered microbes can clean up pollutants; both raise biosafety questions.

**Animal bioreactor:** a transgenic animal that secretes a therapeutic protein into milk, blood, egg white or urine. Milk is preferred because yields are high (g/L) and proteins are glycosylated like human proteins.

rows.en: Prevents clotting in hereditary antithrombin deficiency
**Chicken: human enzymes in egg white (Kanuma, sebelipase α)**

caption.en: Fig. 6. Anand Mohan Chakrabarty’s plasmid-combined _Pseudomonas_: the first patented living organism.

rows.en: Add nutrients to boost native microbes
N and P on oiled shorelines
Supply air to soil or groundwater
Plants take up or degrade pollutants

text.en:
**Bioweapons (concept only)**
• The 1972 Biological Weapons Convention (in force 1975) bans development, production and stockpiling of biological agents as weapons.
• CDC Category A agents (highest priority) include anthrax, smallpox, plague, botulinum toxin, tularaemia and viral haemorrhagic fevers.
• Response relies on surveillance, vaccines, antimicrobials and biosafety/biosecurity rules.
Köhler and Milstein (1975; Nobel 1984) fused a B cell with a myeloma cell to make an immortal antibody factory.

title.en: Molecular Markers: RFLP, RAPD and DNA Fingerprinting

text.en: Markers reveal differences in DNA between individuals, populations and species.

caption.en: Fig. 15. RFLP depends on gain or loss of restriction sites, or insertions and deletions between them.
Fig. 16. RAPD uses one short arbitrary primer.

labels: Random 10-mer primer binds at many sites on both strands (low stringency)
Product only where two primer sites face each other within ~3 kb: amplicon 1
Polymorphism = presence/absence of bands (dominant marker). Quick and cheap but poorly reproducible.
Evidence and Suspect B give identical band patterns: consistent with a match.
Suspect A and the victim differ: excluded as the source.
Modern forensics scores 20 STR loci (CODIS) and gives a random-match probability below 1 in a billion.

text.en:
**Applications of DNA fingerprinting (Alec Jeffreys, 1984)**
• Forensics: identity from blood, semen, hair roots.
• Paternity and kinship; disaster victim identification.
• Wildlife forensics and breed authentication.
• Genetic diversity and mapping in conservation and breeding.
Key points and model answers likely to appear in university examinations.
**Key exam points**
Transgene = promoter + coding sequence + poly(A); microinjection into the **male pronucleus**.
Knockout: ES cells, neo/tk selection, blastocyst injection, chimera, breed; 1:2:1 in F2.
Dolly (1996): SCNT from an adult mammary cell; 277 fusions gave 1 live lamb.
Animal bioreactors secrete drugs in milk (goat antithrombin, rabbit C1-inhibitor).
Superbug (Chakrabarty): Pseudomonas with 4 plasmids; Diamond v. Chakrabarty (1980).
Hybridoma: B cell + HGPRT− myeloma; HAT selects; screen, clone, expand.
-omab, -ximab, -zumab, -umab = murine, chimeric, humanised, human.
Ex vivo vs in vivo gene therapy; CAR-T is ex vivo; oncolytic viruses and suicide genes.
CRISPR: gRNA + Cas9 + NGG PAM; NHEJ vs HDR.
RFLP (co-dominant), RAPD (dominant), STR fingerprinting (forensics).
**Short-answer questions**
Click a question to reveal the model answer.
Q.1Describe the production of a transgenic mouse.▼

A construct (promoter + gene + poly A) is injected into the male pronucleus of fertilised eggs; embryos are transferred to a pseudopregnant foster; pups are screened by PCR/Southern; founders are bred to confirm germ-line transmission.
Q.2How is a knockout mouse produced?▼

A targeting vector with a neo cassette replaces an exon in ES cells by homologous recombination; neo and tk selection enriches targeted cells; they are injected into blastocysts to give chimeras; breeding gives heterozygotes and then homozygous knockouts.
Q.3Explain the cloning of Dolly.▼

A mammary cell from an adult ewe was starved to G0 and fused by electrical pulse with an enucleated egg; the embryo was cultured and transferred to a surrogate; 1 of 277 fusions produced a live lamb in 1996.
Q.4What is the role of HAT medium?▼
Aminopterin blocks de novo nucleotide synthesis, so cells must use the salvage pathway (HGPRT, TK). HGPRT-minus myeloma cells die; unfused B cells die naturally; only hybrids survive.
Q.5Differentiate ex vivo and in vivo gene therapy.▼
Ex vivo: patient cells are modified outside the body and returned. In vivo: the gene vector is injected directly into the patient.
Q.6Write short notes on CRISPR-Cas9.▼
A guide RNA directs Cas9 to a 20-nt target adjacent to an NGG PAM; Cas9 makes a double-strand break; NHEJ gives knockouts and HDR gives precise edits.
Q.7Distinguish RFLP and RAPD.▼
RFLP detects fragment-length differences using restriction enzymes and a probe (co-dominant, reproducible). RAPD uses random primers in PCR (dominant, quick, less reproducible).
